dailyInsight.headline: Audit which environment actually carries your coding agent’s permission choice
dailyInsight.insight: Codex’s fresh turn-environment changes support one bounded audit for teams using multiple roots, remote environments, or delegated agents: trace a single permission profile from selection through the tool that acts, then through one child or resumed task. The source change routes sandboxing, approval, and permission-profile data through the selected turn environment rather than relying only on thread-level defaults; it also materializes project-root rules across that environment’s workspace roots.
dailyInsight.mechanism: One public change snapshots the permission profile into each turn environment and preserves the configuration an active turn captured; the next passes the selected environment’s permissions into shell, unified execution, patching, image viewing, network approval, Guardian context, and delegated-agent paths. The code and tests support a consistency boundary: the authority selected for work should reach the runtime doing that work. They do not turn an allowed action into a safe action or establish behavior outside the inspected source and tests.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: In a multi-workspace or multi-agent task, a good permission UI can still mislead if a different environment executes the command or receives the child task. Treating selected environment, workspace roots, and capture time as reviewable facts gives an operator a specific place to detect authority drift before it becomes a surprising tool call.

actions.audience: Builder or operator supervising multi-root, remote, or delegated coding work
actions.label: Trace one permission handoff
actions.instruction: In a disposable workspace with no production credentials, choose one tool action that could cross a project boundary. Record the selected environment, its workspace roots, its approval and filesystem rules, and whether a child or resumed task inherits that same context. Change only a non-sensitive test policy for a future turn, then verify whether an already-active task keeps its captured configuration. Add a regression test for a secondary root or delegated handoff; do not treat a successful test as proof that the allowed action itself is safe.

receipts.title: Use turn environment permissions for tool execution (#37038)
receipts.supports: Shows that the selected turn environment now supplies sandboxing, approval, and permission-profile data to tool, review, multi-agent, and multi-workspace paths, with focused secondary-root and permission-context tests.

receipts.title: Apply permission profile updates to future turn environments (#37031)
receipts.supports: Shows that environments capture the current profile, retained environments refresh on settings changes, and active turns preserve the configuration they already captured.

confidence.basis: Two fresh merged Codex changes, their implementation paths, and focused tests agree on the narrow environment-bound permission model and on the distinction between active and future turn configuration.

dailyInsight.limitation: These are public source and test receipts from Codex main. They do not establish release availability, a particular local or remote deployment’s configuration, independent security testing, or safety of every action that policy allows.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise this call if public regression evidence shows a selected environment’s tool or child-agent path can silently use another environment’s profile, if project-root rules are not applied to a declared secondary root, or if a documented setting intentionally rewrites active-turn authority mid-flight.
dailyInsight.watchNext: Watch for public tests that change roots or permission settings while remote execution or delegated work is in flight; those cases will show whether the environment boundary stays coherent under handoff and recovery.
